text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed after following the sudden swings in the New York market, traders said. Nearby values managed to claw their way back from the lows in afternoon trade although the spot May contract saw a renewal of bearish sentiment in late trading while other forwards ended slightly firmer. May closed down $1.50 at $309.50 per tonne after hitting an intraday low of $307.40 per tonne and August was up 40 cents at $310.70 per tonne.

Raw sugar future in New York were lifted off the lows hit early by steady short covering by the trade and new fund buying. However, late session trade selling kept prices below unchanged by the close, dealers said. Prices fell in early dealings on trade and then speculative selling. By mid-day, the market had begun to recoup losses with the most active May contract lingering around its previous downside target of 11.00 cents.

Fresh fund buying pushed the most active May contract over the key level to settle at 11.10 cents/lb, down 0.06 cents. March ended 0.15 cents lower at 11.18 cent/lb, while the back months ended unchanged to down 0.03 cents. The last trading day for the spot month is February 28. Despite late-session gains, market sources expect prices to continue their downward momentum.

FRANCE - France produced 4.226 million tonnes of beet white sugar in 1996/97, provisional statistics from the French sugar market intervention board FIRS showed. This compares with 4.199 million tonnes of sugar produced in 1995/96.

In its February report FIRS said an increase in the crop's sugar content helped offset a drought-induced decline in beet weight per ha. The estimate assumed an area of 422,000 ha and a sugar yield of 10.01 tonnes per ha, compared with an area of 430,000 ha and a yield of 9.77 tonnes in 1995/96.

IRELAND - Sugar exports in September 1996 reached 3,830 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 6,648 tonnes. This brought total exports in 1995/96 (October/September) up to 74,907 tonnes against 56,773 tonnes in 1994/95 and 31,867 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in 1995/96 were the United Kingdom with 43,139 tonnes whites against 42,934 tonnes, Israel with 11,914 tonnes, up from 8,731 tonnes and Turkey with 9,999 tonnes compared to nil.

Sugar imports in 1995/96 reached 8,279 tonnes, down from 10,954 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1995/96 were the UK with 3,166 tonnes whites against 3,249 tonnes and France with 2,065 tonnes compared to 2,120 tonnes.

TURKEY - Sugar imports in May 1996 reached 72,849 tonnes, raw value, against nil in May 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (August/May) to 680,761 tonnes compared to 110,334 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 191,885 tonnes against 19,256 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of origin in August May 1995/96 were France with 219,349 tonnes whites against nil, Mexico with 85,607 tonnes compared to nil, the United Kingdom with 64,151 tonnes against 44 tonnes, Brazil with 45,106 tonnes compared to nil and the USA with 44,763 tonnes against nil. Largest raw sugar suppliers in August/May 1995/96 were France with 23,901 tonnes compared to nil, Colombia with 14,564 tonnes against nil and Cuba with 14,000 tonnes against nil.

Sugar exports in August/May 1995/96 amounted to 4,421 tonnes, down from 181,389 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in August/May 1995/96 was Iran with 1,667 tonnes whites, down from 57,241 tonnes.

Iran bought 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar for March/May shipment and 14,000 tonnes of white sugar for April, London traders said. Prices paid were $269 per tonne for the raws and $313 for the whites, it was added. Details of the suppliers have yet to emerge. Earlier this month, Iran bought two 15,000-tonne cargoes of Cuban raw sugar from a London-based trade house at $257 and $258 per tonne for March/April shipment.
